turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
“Doctor, I’ve been feeling very confused lately, and my temperature’s been up. I also have some discomfort in my right upper abdomen, and I’m having trouble explaining it clearly.”
Have you or anyone else noticed a yellowish tint to your eyes or skin recently?
“Doctor, I’m not sure—I can’t really tell if my eyes or skin look yellow, and no one has mentioned anything like that to me.”
Have you felt dizzy, lightheaded, or like you might pass out recently?
“Doctor, I’ve felt lightheaded at times, but I haven’t passed out. I’m mostly just confused and not steady when I try to move around.”
How long have you been experiencing this fever, confusion, and abdominal discomfort?

“Doctor, the confusion has been getting noticeably worse over the past couple of days, and the fever and right upper abdominal discomfort started around the same time, though I can’t be certain of the exact day.”
Have you experienced any severe shaking chills or shivering along with your fever?
“Doctor, I’ve had a fever and I feel quite unwell, but I don’t recall any severe shaking chills or intense shivering.”

“Doctor, I’ve never been told I have gallstones to my knowledge, and I don’t recall any prior gallbladder problems. I’m mostly just confused and uncomfortable in my right upper abdomen, with a fever that seems to be getting worse.”
Have you had any burning or pain when you urinate, or have you noticed any changes in how often you need to urinate?
“Doctor, I haven’t noticed any burning when I urinate, and I’m not sure about changes in how often I’m going—I’ve been too confused to pay close attention.”
Have you had any nausea or vomiting since these symptoms started?
“Doctor, I don’t recall any nausea or vomiting, though my appetite and comfort have been poor and I’ve been too confused to track it carefully.”

“Doctor, I’m not sure—my hospice nurse or family would know whether my long-term illness is cancer. If you ask them, I think they can tell you the diagnosis and any recent changes to my medications.”
